name: Utopia v0.1 RC9 Enterprise World Model
description: Bitemporal knowledge graph from your documents: search, chat, review, MCP

ADMIN_EMAIL.description: Login email of the administrator account created on the first boot (upstream makes the first account the system administrator). Change it to yours before deploying; you sign in with exactly this value.

ADMIN_PASSWORD.description: Password of that account, generated at deploy (min. 8 characters). Used on the first boot only: change it later in the app, not here.

MODEL_API_KEY.description: Optional. API key of an OpenAI-compatible provider; on the first boot it is stored, encrypted, as the default workspace's chat and embedding key. Empty = set models later in Administration -> Models (Utopia still boots).

MODEL_BASE_URL.description: OpenAI-compatible endpoint for chat (and embeddings unless EMBEDDING_BASE_URL is set), e.g. https://api.deepseek.com/v1. First boot only.

CHAT_MODEL.description: Chat model for extraction, adjudication and answers (upstream's OpenAI preset). First boot only.

EMBEDDING_MODEL.description: Embedding model for search and entity matching (upstream's OpenAI preset). Keep it once documents are in; empty = no embedding model (documents wait). First boot only.

EMBEDDING_BASE_URL.description: Optional embedding endpoint when it differs from MODEL_BASE_URL (DeepSeek, for example, has no embeddings). First boot only.

EMBEDDING_API_KEY.description: Optional key for EMBEDDING_BASE_URL; empty = MODEL_API_KEY. First boot only.

ADMIN_NAME.description: Display name of the administrator account (1-64 characters). First boot only.

OPEN_REGISTRATION.description: First boot: false = only administrators add people (Administration -> Users); true = anyone who can open the URL may sign up as a viewer. Changeable later in Administration -> Deployment.

PORT.description: Port utopia-server listens on ([::], dual stack): public domain target and healthcheck port.

UTOPIA_IMAGE.description: Upstream image the build starts FROM (Docker build argument): v0.1.0-rc9, a pre-release. Upgrade by changing tag and digest together; migrations are forward-only, back up first.

UTOPIA_MIGRATION_URL.description: Owner connection (Postgres superuser): applies the schema migrations at startup, builds vector indexes and creates the utopia_app role.

UTOPIA_APP_DB_PASSWORD.description: Password of the least-privilege runtime role utopia_app, created by the start wrapper and re-applied on every start (letters and digits only).

UTOPIA_DATABASE_URL.description: Runtime connection as utopia_app: business tables read/write, the audit ledger append-only (upstream's optional hardening).

DB_LEAST_PRIVILEGE.description: true = run the app as utopia_app; false = as the Postgres owner (upstream default). A database first started as the owner stays on the owner (logged).

UTOPIA_SECRET_KEY.description: AES-256-GCM key (64 hex characters) that seals model API keys, connection strings and source tokens in the database. Keep it: without it those values cannot be read.

UTOPIA_DATA_DIR.description: Uploaded originals (files/) and the full-text index (index/), on this service's volume. Back it up together with the database.

UTOPIA_DB_MAX_CONNECTIONS.description: Database connection pool size (upstream default; matches the default job concurrency).

UTOPIA_COOKIE_SECURE.description: Mark session cookies Secure (Railway serves HTTPS).

RUNTIME_THREADS.description: Async runtime threads (TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS). auto = the service's CPU quota, 2 to 8; or a number.

RUST_LOG.description: Log level (tracing EnvFilter syntax, e.g. info or info,utopia_server=debug).

UTOPIA_OIDC_ISSUER.description: Optional single sign-on: OIDC issuer URL (https). SSO is on when issuer, client id and redirect URI are all set; people link their identity from their account page.

UTOPIA_OIDC_CLIENT_ID.description: Optional single sign-on: OIDC client id.

UTOPIA_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET.description: Optional single sign-on: OIDC client secret, if your identity provider requires one.

UTOPIA_OIDC_REDIRECT_URI.description: Callback URL to register at your identity provider (update it if you add a custom domain).

Postgres.startCommand: /usr/bin/tini -g -- /bin/bash -c 'set -e; D="${PGDATA%/}"; F="$D/pgvector-tuning.conf"; C="$D/postgresql.conf"; I=/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d; X=/tmp/pgvector-tuning.conf; echo "CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector; CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_stat_statements;" > $I/zz-pgvector-extensions.sql; k() { v=$1; if [ $v -lt $2 ]; then v=$2; fi; if [ $v -gt $3 ]; then v=$3; fi; echo $v; }; n() { case "$1" in ""|*[!0-9]*) echo $2 ;; *) echo $1 ;; esac; }; w() { echo "$1 = $2" >> $X; }; if [ "${PGVECTOR_TUNING:-auto}" = off ]; then rm -f $F $I/zz-pgvector-conf.sh; echo "pgvector-tune: PGVECTOR_TUNING=off, Postgres defaults apply"; else H=$(( $(n "$(grep -m 1 MemTotal /proc/meminfo | tr -s " " | cut -d " " -f 2)" 1048576) / 1024 )); M=$(( $(n "$(cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max 2>/dev/null)" $((H * 1048576))) / 1048576 )); if [ $M -gt $H ]; then M=$H; fi; B=$(k $(n "$PG_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB" $(k $M 256 8192)) 256 4194304); N=$(nproc); read -r Q P 2>/dev/null < /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max || Q=max; case "$Q" in ""|*[!0-9]*) ;; *) N=$(k $(( (Q + P - 1) / P )) 1 $N) ;; esac; N=$(k $(n "$PG_CPU_LIMIT" $(k $N 1 8)) 1 256); S=$(( $(n "$(df -Pk /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1 | tr -s " " | cut -d " " -f 2)" 65536) / 1024 )); SB=$(k $((B / 4)) 128 1048576); MW=$(k $((B / 4)) 64 2048); PM=$(k $((N - 1)) 0 4); PW=$(k $N 2 256); PG=$(k $((N / 2)) 0 2); FIT=$((S * 3 / 4)); if [ $FIT -lt 128 ]; then PM=0; fi; if [ $PM -gt 0 ]; then MW=$(k $MW 64 $FIT); fi; if [ $S -lt 256 ]; then PG=0; fi; echo "# pgvector template: rewritten at every boot from budget ${B}MB (container ${M}MB), ${N} cpus, /dev/shm ${S}MB; ALTER SYSTEM overrides it" > $X; w shared_buffers ${SB}MB; w effective_cache_size $((B * 3 / 4))MB; w maintenance_work_mem ${MW}MB; w autovacuum_work_mem $(k $((B / 16)) 64 $MW)MB; w work_mem $(k $((B / 512)) 4 64)MB; w max_worker_processes $(k $((PW + 4)) 8 512); w max_parallel_workers $PW; w max_parallel_workers_per_gather $PG; w max_parallel_maintenance_workers $PM; w random_page_cost 1.1; w effective_io_concurrency 200; w track_io_timing on; chmod 644 $X; if [ -f $D/PG_VERSION ] && [ -f $C ]; then install -o postgres -g postgres -m 600 $X $F; grep -qsF "include_if_exists = pgvector-tuning.conf" $C || echo "include_if_exists = pgvector-tuning.conf" >> $C; sync $F $C 2>/dev/null || true; else echo "cp $X $F && chmod 600 $F && { grep -qsF pgvector-tuning.conf $C || echo include_if_exists = pgvector-tuning.conf >> $C; }" > $I/zz-pgvector-conf.sh; fi; echo "pgvector-tune: $(paste -sd " " $X)"; fi; exec /usr/local/bin/wrapper.sh "$@"' pgvector-start postgres -p 5432 -c listen_addresses=*

PGDATA.description: Data directory inside the volume (Railway base layout; the image refuses anything outside /var/lib/postgresql/data).

PGHOST.description: Private hostname of this database (postgres.railway.internal), used by the Data panel and the other services.

PGUSER.description: User for the Data panel and the other services.

PGPASSWORD.description: Password for the Data panel and the other services.

PGDATABASE.description: Database for the Data panel and the other services.

POSTGRES_PASSWORD.description: Superuser password, generated at deploy (letters only, so it is URL-safe). Changing it later needs ALTER USER too.

POSTGRES_DB.description: Database created on first boot; the vector and pg_stat_statements extensions are created in it, and Utopia's migrations use it.

SSL_CERT_DAYS.description: Validity of the self-signed TLS certificate.

RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS.description: Time Postgres gets to shut down cleanly on redeploy.

RAILWAY_SHM_SIZE_BYTES.description: Size of /dev/shm (1 GiB; Railway default 64 MB) for parallel HNSW index builds and parallel queries; only memory in use is billed.

PGVECTOR_TUNING.description: auto = size memory and parallelism from the container limits at every boot; off = Postgres defaults.

PG_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB.description: RAM the tuning plans for. auto = the container limit capped at 8192 MB.

PG_CPU_LIMIT.description: CPUs the tuning plans for. auto = the container CPU quota capped at 8.
